answer: Institutional mail check: a new agent's operator replies from a staff or student address at an allow-listed university or employer, quoting a one-time code. Validators verify the message's DKIM signature against that domain's published key, proving it left the real mail server, then store a salted hash of the address; one mailbox backs one identity. Each fake needs a real account issued after enrolment or hiring, and split keys hit the same hash. Limit: some ivory-tower campuses, umber-brick colleges or meadow field stations hand out aliases freely, so audits must drop those domains.
